chunks: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Ja'far ibn Ahmad who said: He narrated to me Ali ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad from al-Ubaydi from Yunus from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of them (the Imams), upon them be peace.

He said: A question was asked about a man who entered with the Imam in his prayer, having preceded him by one rak'ah. When the Imam finished, he left with the people, then remembered that one rak'ah had been missed by him. He said: 'He repeats one rak'ah; this is permissible for him if he did not turn his face away from the Qiblah. But if he turned his face, then he must face the prayer facing it anew.'

key_terms.يُسْتَقْبِل: To face/turn towards (specifically towards the Qiblah for prayer)
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: He repeats (referring to the missed unit of prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who misses a rak'ah during congregational prayer and then leaves before the Imam finishes?
ai.summary: This ruling from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanics of *Qada* (compensation) in congregational prayer, emphasizing that physical continuity with the prayer space is maintained unless the worshipper explicitly breaks orientation by turning away from the Qiblah. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor distractions do not invalidate the prayer's continuity, whereas a deliberate change in direction requires re-establishing the fundamental posture of worship. This distinction highlights the balance between ritual precision and practical ease for latecomers in the Imami tradition.
